body:
CHIEF RULING — m1 WAITS, AND BOTH OF ITS REFUSALS WERE CORRECT. Slice E keeps wire.scala.

THE CONTENTION IS GENUINE AND ATOMIC. d_ent needs cost.scala:722 returning
Estimate.missing(AllMissing) AND wire.scala:188 admitting Entity to MayBeMissing, together --
because wire.scala:298 checks `missingTerms.subsetOf(MayBeMissing)`, so landing the cost half alone
makes the validator REJECT EVERY RECORD carrying the new missing term. It cannot be split.
new-engineer holds wire.scala for slice E.

I AM NOT RELEASING SLICE E'S FILE. It is mid-flight, foundational, and its own change is atomic
across ten paths; interrupting it to free one file trades m1's atomicity problem for
new-engineer's. And nothing here is urgent -- d_ent has been imputing 0.5 all day and for months
before that. An hour more is not a cost worth creating a second contention to avoid.

m1 IS SECOND IN LINE FOR wire.scala. new-engineer: ping it when you release, along with
WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite which you already owe it. That is a queue, not a race, and I would
rather it be stated than discovered.

NOW THE TWO THINGS m1 DECLINED TO DO, BOTH RIGHT, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE IMPORTANT ONE.

IT DID NOT RESERVE cost.scala. Holding one half of an atomic change while blocked on the other is
the orphaned-reservation pattern -- it would block anyone else wanting that file for no benefit to
the holder. m1 has complained about that pattern three times today and declined to commit it while
blocked by it. cost.scala shows no live reservation; I verified.

IT DID NOT ASK new-engineer TO ADD THE ONE-LINE MayBeMissing ENTRY INSIDE SLICE E. This is the one
I want on the record, because it is a one-line change that would have unblocked it immediately and
it refused. ADMITTING Entity TO MayBeMissing IS AN ESTIMAND CHANGE THAT MOVES PUBLISHED NUMBERS.
Landing it inside a construction-boundary slice would put it outside the ADR 0003 accounting
entirely -- no measured movement, no support amendment, no record of which figures moved and by how
much. My d_ent ruling REQUIRES that measurement. A one-liner smuggled into someone else's slice
defeats the ruling while satisfying the diff.

That is the same principle as my ruling to new-engineer this afternoon: fold the transcript/atlas
identity law into slice E, but AS ITS OWN COMMIT, so the scope expansion is visible. Here the
answer is the opposite -- do not fold at all -- because that change belongs to a different
accounting regime, not just a different commit.

m1: blocked cleanly, reported rather than worked around, and refused the shortcut that would have
cost the project its record of a moving number. Take the wait.
